newsitem.title: USA: Republicans take legal steps over Democratic funds.
newsitem.headline: Republicans take legal steps over Democratic funds.

text.p: Republicans said on Tuesday they would take legal action against President Bill Clinton's Democratic Party over alleged campaign financing violations, amid reports Democrats had taken improper foreign donations.

A week before the Nov. 5 presidential election, Republican Party Chairman Haley Barbour said his party would ask a federal court for an injunction to freeze Democratic spending until they file an overdue report on donations and spending.

The controversy erupted after Democrats initially said they would not be filing a report on the party's contributions and expenditures for the first two weeks of October with the Federal Election Commission.
With Clinton trying to maintain his commanding lead in the polls, Democrats scrambled to limit the damage.

Democratic Party Chairman Christopher Dodd, a senator from Connecticut, said in a statement the party was not legally required to file a financial report before the election but would give the Federal Election Commission "raw data" on its contributions and spending anyway. He said it would then provide an official final report sometime later.
A Democratic official said "about 500 pages" of statistics would be sent to the FEC late Tuesday.

A sceptical Barbour, Dodd's Republican counterpart, said on CNN he did not expect to see the final report until after the election. There was no indication the Democratic gesture would lead Republicans to withdraw their legal challenge.
Earlier, Dodd said the decision not to file the report by last Thursday's deadline had been made by staff members.

"If you don't make contributions then you don't legally have to file a report and so some staff made that decision. In my view they were wrong, you should file it even if you don't have expenditures because we're in that kind of environment," he told CNN.

Barbour has suggested the failure to disclose the finances suggested the Democrats were hiding something. "What are they hiding that they don't want to comply with the law?" he asked in a telephone conference with reporters earlier on Tuesday.

He later told a news conference: "To make sure the law is in force, the Republican National Committee will file a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking a temporary restraining order that would freeze all Democratic National Committee assets and prevent the DNC from expending any funds (on the election) until the FEC report is filed as required by law."
The row follows news reports that Clinton's campaign was taking questionable contributions from people linked to financial interests in Indonesia, South Korea and Taiwan.

Dole, struggling to narrow Clinton's lead, has seized on the issue, peppering his speeches with allegations that the president improperly took money from foreigners keen to influence administration policy.

The Justice Department is looking into reports that the chairman of the American Institute in Taiwan -- the U.S. diplomatic link with Taiwan -- urged Taiwanese businessmen to contribute to Clinton's re-election campaign.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the issue was turned over to Justice after the allegations against James Wood, a former White House aide, were reported to the State Department's Office of Inspector General.

Meanwhile John Huang, a key figure in allegations of improper Democratic Party fund-raising from Indonesian interests, was questioned in a civil suit by a conservative group seeking information about Huang's activities while he was a Commerce Department official.

Huang has come under fire over the legality of contributions he solicited as a fundraiser but those activities are not at issue in the civil lawsuit and the judge limited his questioning to the subject of the civil suit.
Huang, a one-time official of the giant Indonesian Lippo Group, has helped raise large sums of money from Asian Americans, including those with ties to Indonesian interests.
Allegations of improper donations have not been been limited only to Democrats, and there have also been news reports of Dole taking thousands of dollars from Cuban American sugar interests.
Dodd said Republican finances should be closely examined.
